_note: Prose shared by every HELHEST v2 release (Odin1 + Fixposition rig); a release spec names it with "inherit". Migrated 2026-10-12 from HELHEST_v2_4/manifest.json.

cloud_frame.chain: base_link -> odin1_base_link (the robot URDF, (0.10, 0, 0.10), identity rotation, the same in every bag) -> imu_link (identity) -> odin1_lidar (PINNED, below)
cloud_frame.pinned: The Odin1 publishes imu_link -> odin1_lidar and odin1_lidar -> odin1_camera_link on /tf_static as a running estimate, not a calibration: across 42 bags of the 2026-09-14 firmware the lidar-to-IMU translation spans about 3 cm per axis between the 10th and 90th percentile and half a degree of pitch, and it changes within a bag. Since dataset_tools f90c4c5 the extractor replaces both edges with one constant for every bag, the per-axis median of what the driver published (dataset_tools/tf_pins.py; the per-bag survey is docs/odin_tf_static_2026-09-30.txt): lidar in IMU (0.011, 0.024, 0.006) m, roll/pitch/yaw (-0.29, -0.53, 0.12) deg; camera in lidar (-0.010, 0.039, 0.014) m, (0.40, 0.04, 0.06) deg. Each scene records under tf_pins.txt what its bag had published; the distance between that and the pin is under scenes.*.odin_tf_bag_vs_pin (largest lidar offset in this root: 35 mm; scenes flagged far, i.e. over 30 mm or 1 deg: 0014). So the lidar sits (0.111, 0.024, 0.106) m from base_link in every scene of this root. v2.0 and v2.1 used each bag's own value. The pin is the driver's estimate with its wandering removed, NOT a measurement: the user measured the centre of the Odin housing about 0.136 m above base_link, and the lidar ground still reads 4-5 cm above the wheel bottoms (open_items).
cloud_frame.clouds: what the Odin1 published, transformed by that chain; nothing removed but NaN rows and all-zero points
cloud_frame.deskew: Every sweep is motion-compensated onto data_ts: p_ref = R(t_ref)^T (R(t_p) p + x(t_p) - x(t_ref)), t_p = stamp + offset_time, poses from /odin1/odometry (lerp + slerp), the rotation inside the sweep from /odin1/imu where it agrees with the slerp to 1 deg (99.8 % of sweeps). Sweeps the odometry does not bracket (the first or last of a bag) are written as recorded and counted in extract_meta.json frames.deskew.no_pose.

cloud_dtype: float32 x, y, z, intensity; NaN rows and all-zero points dropped at extraction, nothing else -- the robot's own returns are in the clouds. 14-28k points per frame (Lipník the sparsest, the Temešvár forest track the densest).

odometry.source: /odin1/odometry: the Odin1's lidar-inertial odometry, 14.46 Hz, 6-DoF, stamped on the same clock as its clouds and images (stamp = image stamp), re-expressed at base_link through odin1_base_link -> base_link ((0.10, 0, 0.10), identity rotation)
odometry.frame: base_link, anchored per segment at the identity: each segment of odometry_segments.txt starts at eye(4) at its first pose and is integrated from there, so its frame carries whatever attitude the robot had at that pose and is NOT levelled against gravity (z is up only if the robot started level). Use it for relative motion within a segment (T0^-1 Ti), never across segments and never as an absolute attitude or height: absolute roll/pitch is gravity_align.npy, position and heading are gps.npy. Two segments start upside down: defects.odometry_frame_upside_down.
odometry.contract: segments in odometry_segments.txt MUST NOT be bridged -- each is re-anchored to its own first pose
odometry.segmentation: gaps > 1 s and jumps (the Odin1's relocalisations, max_speed 6.0 m/s); one-sample spikes are discarded rather than split. Each segment's reason names why THAT segment ended: gap, teleport, end_of_run. Segments are NUMBERED FROM 1.
odometry.check: pose_check.txt per scene (and extract_meta.json frames.pose_check): the odometry against /fixposition/odometry_enu at base_link -- spans, path and jumps in each, z range, clock lag, roll/pitch difference, |displacement| disagreement over 1/2/5 s windows. Measured on 0009: 2.1 / 3.4 / 4.6 cm median over 1 / 2 / 5 s, scale 0.994, clock lag +14 ms (the Odin1 clock against GNSS time). Scenes whose check carries a WARNING are listed per scene below (pose_check_vs_fixposition.warnings).
odometry.history: v2 beta to v2.2 took the ground truth from /fixposition/odometry_enu (GNSS/INS, 10 Hz); decision 2026-10-01 (user): the Odin1 odometry is the ground truth, the Fixposition the georeference and the check.
odometry.seams_added_2026_10_01: Four relocalisation corrections of the Odin1 odometry too small for the 6 m/s gate were made segment seams after the extraction, the new segments re-anchored to the identity (odometry.txt rewritten atomically): 0000 pose 11199 (t+775.3 s, 26.9 cm kink in one 71 ms step), 0006 pose 10006 (t+986.9 s, 17.0 cm), 0016 poses 3381 (t+233.7 s, 14.6 cm) and 3710 (t+256.4 s, 9.3 cm, borderline). Found by odin_step_audit.txt (odometry vs the GNSS fixes per step) and attributed by the second difference of the Odin1's own track: a genuine correction is a kink in it, a GNSS blip leaves it smooth. About 45 of the ~50 flagged steps were the GNSS's (multipath, fix jitter, settling at a scene start) and are left as they are; the audit file stands as recorded. transforms.npy is unsegmented and unchanged. (Fix DRIFT session, DRIFT issues 38/39.)
odometry.frame_correction: Rotated onto the cloud frame on 2026-10-06: corrections.odom_frame_2026_10_06.

gravity_align: Ry(pitch) @ Rx(roll) of the base from the /odin1/odometry attitude at each data_ts (v2.2: the Fixposition INS). pose_check.txt reports the median roll/pitch difference between the two per scene (0009: 0.25 / 1.13 deg); the Fixposition's ~2 deg pitch against base_link noted in v2.2 is therefore partly the receiver's. Since 2026-10-06 the attitude of the CLOUD frame: the Odin1 attitude rotated by the per-scene odom_frame correction (corrections.odom_frame_2026_10_06); pose_check.txt still reports the uncorrected difference.

camera.distortion_model: equidistant (fisheye, 4 coefficients) -- v1 was rational_polynomial on a pinhole; anything that unprojects has to change
camera.extrinsic: T_cam_to_base.txt, p_base = T @ p_cam_optical, from tf_static; taken against the image's own header.frame_id (odin1_camera_link)
camera.extrinsic_caveat: odin1_camera_link is already optical-convention; its child odin1_camera_link_optical_frame applies the optical rotation a second time and points 90 deg off. Never look up the _optical_frame. The extrinsic value itself is unvalidated -- a checkerboard at 1-2 m would settle it.
camera.occlusion: The robot's own front wheels permanently occlude roughly 10 % of every frame (two arcs, lower left and lower right) -- precisely the near-field terrain the wheels are about to cross. In the Lipník scenes a Bluetooth antenna (for follow-me scenarios, green in the images) sits in front of the chassis and the lidar sees it at r 0.2-0.5 m, ~900 points per frame; the height maps cut everything inside 0.65 m. In the Lipník scenes a Bluetooth antenna (for follow-me scenarios, green in the images) sits in front of the chassis and the lidar sees it at r 0.2-0.5 m, ~900 points per frame; the height maps cut everything inside 0.65 m.
camera.exposure: The Temešvár meadow was driven into a low sun (0008-0010, 0014): heavy flare and a washed-out sky in many frames. The 2026-09-29 session runs from late afternoon into dusk: low sun in 0016-0018, a flat white sky in 0019-0021.
camera.frame_rate: camera and lidar 1:1 at the Odin's nominal 15 Hz in every scene (median 69 ms between frames). This is the fixed driver of 2026-09-14; the doubled images of the beta's first two sessions do not occur here.

gps.file: gps.npy, (M, 8): t, lat, lon, alt, status, cov_ee, cov_nn, cov_uu
gps.role: present in every scene; comparison and mapping only
gps.status_values: -1 NO_FIX, 0 FIX, 2 GBAS_FIX (RTK). Most scenes are predominantly GBAS_FIX. Exceptions: see defects.gnss_no_rtk.

images.encoding: camera JPEG bytes verbatim, msg.data unmodified
images.resolution: 1600x1296, baseline JPEG, 4:2:0, quality about 95, as the Odin1 publishes it; about 0.7 MB per frame
images.provenance: Written by the extractor (--image_format camera, the default since ef1fce4): the bytes of the sensor_msgs/CompressedImage message, unmodified, under the extension their first bytes name. The extractor decodes each image once to check it. PIL and OpenCV decode them to the same pixels; a scene of v2.1 decodes to the same pixels frame for frame where the frame sets agree.
images.consumers: a consumer reads images.extension and refuses a root whose files are not what it declares; a root without the key holds PNG

not_present.regen: no regen/ directory: no offline odometry stage on this rig

odom_frame.what: odometry.txt, transforms.npy and gravity_align.npy of every scene rotated onto the frame of the scene's clouds (dataset_tools.odom_frame, dataset_tools 222d587); per scene in scenes.*.odom_frame_deg and <scene>/odom_frame.txt. Clouds, images and every other file of the extraction are unchanged.
odom_frame.why: The Odin1 computes /odin1/odometry with its own running lidar-to-IMU estimate, not the pinned constant the clouds go through (tf_pins.txt), so the pose frame and the cloud frame of one scene sat apart by up to 0.8 deg. gravity_align.npy is the pose frame's attitude, so the clouds were levelled with the wrong tilt, and every height map tilted against the driven path: DRIFT's path-vs-map slope guard (scripts/analysis/check_path_vs_map_slope.py, limit 0.03 in dz/ds) read 0.056 on v2.3 (2026-10-06, reported by the DRIFT session).
odom_frame.how: Clouds 1.4-3 s apart registered by point-to-plane ICP (open3d) in the cloud frame against the same motion in the pose frame, up to 600 pairs per scene. Pitch: the median difference in elevation of the direction of travel. Roll: Kabsch over translation directions and rotation axes, used when its bootstrap sd is under 0.15 deg (every scene but 0012). Yaw not applied. Poses T -> X^T T X (positions unchanged, the anchored first pose still the identity); gravity_align from the corrected attitude.
